## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (≥4000) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963, so the curve starts in the L2-resident regime. At q=0, cost FALLS from 6.697 ns/p (N=4000) to 5.705 ns/p (N=65000) — pure overhead amortization as per-particle fixed costs dilute across more particles. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces only a mild knee: ns/p RISES from 5.705 (N=65000) to 6.137 (N=4000000), a 7.5% degradation, indicating the working set streams without a sharp cliff. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: at q=0.25 the cost is FLAT at ~11.05–11.12 ns/p across all N, and at q=0.5 it is FLAT at ~13.1–13.4 ns/p. The small-N spike reappears at high death rates (12.753 ns/p at N=4000, q=0.1; 15.316 at q=0.5) because respawn overhead cannot amortize across few particles.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 11.92 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.0 — 47.3% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0 the cell holds 44–47% of ceiling across all N with no clear transition, meaning it is bandwidth-limited but far from saturating DRAM. Death rate drives a steady collapse: 9.02 GB/s (36%) at q=0.01, 8.23 GB/s (33%) at q=0.05, 7.55 GB/s (30%) at q=0.1, 6.15 GB/s (24%) at q=0.25, and 5.07 GB/s (20%) at q=0.5. The transition from bandwidth-limited to overhead-bound occurs by q=0.05, where the branchy respawn and render-scatter costs dominate and further death-rate increases no longer track a bandwidth relationship.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. The hot loop loads one particle's data with `ldr q1, [x25]` (4 floats) and `ldr d2, [x25, #0x10]` (2 floats), then uses `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` to rearrange and `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]` to insert a scalar, packing components into a 4-lane vector for `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0`. A gather-like `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads the fifth component into a lane, followed by `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` pairs. This per-particle vectorization on stride-68 data explains the 47% ceiling: each particle is processed individually with no cross-particle streaming. The render path's `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular pixel stores (16 `strb` instructions) with 18 `csel` and 7 `fcmp` for branchless respawn further cap bandwidth as death rate rises.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0 the cell peaks at 11.92 GB/s = 47% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, never approaching streaming saturation. The component-wise auto-vectorization with `ld1.s` gather and per-particle `ldr q` loads processes one 68-byte particle at a time, preventing cross-particle streaming; the 47% figure holds flat across N, confirming a structural rather than cache-induced limit. Death rate compounds this: by q=0.5 bandwidth falls to 5.07 GB/s (20% of ceiling) as the byte-granular render scatter and respawn overhead dominate.
